"Fivefold and tenfold price targets are algebraic hurdles, not forecasts. At today’s shares, they require equity values five and ten times approximately ₹97.96 crore before considering new capital. Each target is translated into EBIT, revenue, implied five-year revenue CAGR and ONWC at 29% of sales, followed by a linked monthly funding simulation. A target that breaches cash has no ordinary return, even if its terminal P&L looks attractive. The simple algebra takes no terminal-cash credit; the separate cash model tests the full operating path. No fabricated addressable-market estimate is used to certify that such growth is possible.

Evidence against the thesis includes the limited moat, rising overdue balances, uncertain loan terms, poor cumulative cash conversion and very short order visibility. Evidence that would change the conclusion is sustained cash conversion through multiple reporting periods, independently verified advances recovery, stable margins without increasingly generous credit, transparent overseas returns and executable market liquidity. At an analytical normalized corporate tax rate of 25.168%, distinct from FY26 reported effective tax of approximately 26.74%, three-year NOPAT growth of ₹7.2559 crore divided by IC growth of ₹15.9557 crore gives 45.48%. Latest incremental NOPAT of ₹1.8424 crore divided by ₹5.8384 crore additional IC gives 31.56%; FY26 average-capital ROIC is 59.67%. The latest IC increase reconciles to capex less depreciation, change in ONWC and gratuity without a material unexplained residual. A lagged denominator using FY24–25 capital growth gives 25.13%. All are accounting proxies, not project IRRs. [financial_calculations]

"The ordinary bear path breaches the required cash floor during the first monthly supplier-prepayment stage, before later collections. It is stopped at that stage. No ordinary terminal price, CAGR or hurdle entry is reported after that breach. This is an analytical stress result, not evidence that the actual issuer has defaulted.

A separate rescue branch assumes fresh equity at 70% of the reference price, ₹46.865 per share, a 3% issuance cost and an additional ₹2 crore cash buffer. Whole shares are rounded up. The branch needs 692,101 new shares, about ₹3.2435 crore gross and ₹3.1462 crore net, diluting existing holders by approximately 4.52%. No investor, bank or promoter has committed this financing. It is not a recommendation to issue shares and cannot be used as ordinary downside protection. With that rescue the terminal price is about ₹30.51 and five-year return about −14.54%. The ordinary case remains unvalued after failure. [MODEL]

A separate asset-recovery test haircuts March receivables, prepaids, vendor/staff advances, loans and PPE, while settling disclosed operating, tax and debt claims plus the company tax contingency. It gives about ₹3.47 or ₹0 per current diluted share before legal costs and timing. It excludes unverified remaining IPO cash and is not a legal liquidation waterfall. Its role is to show why accounting net worth is not automatically a reliable price floor.

Important bear mechanisms are slower client collections, advance-payment losses, event cancellations, supplier concentration, international setup spending before revenue, operating-margin compression and illiquid execution. A stock-price decline alone is not thesis failure; sustained collection shortfalls or unexplained capital transfers would be. D3 reflects weak demonstrable protection, not a claim that all assets are worthless."

Forecast periods are five rolling twelve-month years after 20 October 2026, not mislabeled fiscal years. Cash taxes follow EBIT less interest, depreciation is added back, total capex and incremental ONWC consume cash, debt principal is repaid in a separately labelled month-8 stress and no refinancing is automatic. Earmarked IPO funds are released only against positive eligible working-capital deployment. Each month first funds a temporary vendor prepayment and permanent outflows before the later operating collections arrive. That intraperiod test prevents annual cash balances from concealing a funding failure.

Base growth is 15%, 15%, 12%, 10% and 8%, with EBIT margins 13%, 13.5%, 14%, 14% and 14%; the terminal cash-rent EBIT multiple is 6. Bull growth is 25%, 25%, 20%, 18%, 15% with a 16% margin and multiple8. Bear growth is −15%, 0%, 3%, 5%, 5%, margins 5–8%, working capital at 45% of sales, a ₹2 crore noncollection cash stress and multiple4. These are analyst assumptions, not guidance. Rent remains in cash operating costs and no invented lease liability is subtracted.

The conditional base terminal price is about ₹123.64 and return 13.05%; conditional bull is about ₹238.65 and 28.94%. Base 12%, 15% and 18% hurdle entries are approximately ₹70.16, ₹61.47 and ₹54.04. They are scenario outputs, not a live fair-value recommendation. A 15% constant-growth reverse test at multiple6 requires about 15.19% annual revenue growth; at multiple4 it requires about 25.87%. Each solution is checked through its cash path, not solved using earnings alone. Terminal equity adds only cash above the minimum liquidity floor and unused earmark, then subtracts debt and divides by actual or rescued diluted claims. No intercorporate-loan recovery is casually added as cash.

The complete model includes annual and monthly rows, the March-to-entry bridge, growth/multiple sensitivity, current-cash-use/working-capital sensitivity, other-bank availability stress, 12/15/18% reverse hurdles and funded multibagger tests. The canonical record embeds every published table and linked scenario path. Unknown current cash makes R and P NS even though the conditional model is numerically complete."

Customer diversification improved substantially. The top ten represented 46.42% of FY23 revenue, 37.59% in FY24 and 19.25% in FY25; the eleven-month February 2026 figure was 22.66%. The largest FY25 client was only 3.67%. This weakens single-client risk, but does not demonstrate a price premium, patent barrier or contractual annuity. Supplier concentration moves the other way in the latest partial period: top ten suppliers were 65.94% and the largest 21.23%. [prospectus]

Repeat-client counts were 48, 28, 27 and 63 across FY23, FY24, FY25 and the eleven-month period. Without cohort denominators, churn and customer revenues, these cannot become retention percentages. Management experience and design portfolios are advantages, but no independent win/loss study, sustained same-project pricing premium or exclusive venue franchise is available. MOAT 4 recognizes coordination skill without promoting it into a durable structural barrier. A material improvement would require recurring multi-event contracts, verified repeat-customer economics, stable vendor terms and margins maintained through a slowdown."
